input.quote: the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual and set at the greater of USD 100,000 and 12 months' charges, and the consequential-damages exclusion is mutual, so the basis is acceptable. However it fails the fallback on carve-outs: only indemnification payments and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the cap, with nothing for breach of confidentiality/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and Section 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability for loss of or damage to our data entirely. We added an Excluded Claims paragraph; the USD 100,000 floor (vs our USD 1,000,000 preference) is noted but not separately flagged.

input.quote: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and is related, directly or indirectly, to the Services; or
input.rationale: IBM's IP indemnity in Section 8.1 is present with the usual exclusions and procure/modify/replace/credit remedies, which meets the fallback. But Section 8.2(a)(3) requires us to indemnify IBM for any Services Recipient claim relating directly or indirectly to IBM's own Services — a one-way Customer indemnity for the Vendor's services, which is walk-away territory. Redline carves out claims arising from IBM's acts, omissions or breach; the 12-month credit cap on the IP remedy is noted but not separately flagged.
